I was very busy and stressed at my own job. Meanwhile, phoned the practice for appointment. Here's the problem: if you are going to quickly snap down the phone, eg "see physio at 10.40" then promptly hang up, then I am now very busy at my job, having to negotiate with managers and other teams to get away, AND trying to remember the time I was quoted over the poor noisy phone line. So amongst all the cancelling of meetings and renegotiation of deadlines AND getting quickly ready to rush to the practice in 30 mins, I might get the time I was quoted a bit wrong by 5 mins, eg was it 10:40 or 10:45? This is your fault KMP, because the system you run means there is no written confirmation not even a text confirmation - it is purely my memory of the time quoted versus the version by the desk staff. So if I am 5 mins out, I think that your staff should be more professional and not throw a childish strop and fall out with me, then say horrible things to me like accusing of saying things I didn't actually say, just to score points and look superior.
I feel like I should have a sign round MY neck saying that I HAVE A ZERO VERBAL ABUSE POLICY. It works both ways - you can't get all personal and say horrible things to me if I'm running all over the place, stressed, and trying to get to my appointment with no written confirmation of the time. Then when I protect myself or try to argue my side of the story I get abused. Then I bet your staff put a secret code by my name to say I am a difficult liar. Why does trying to get a medical appointment, or trying to get a prescription as promised, always turn into an aggressive, hostile, demeaning, unpleasant experience?
I am stressed out at my job and handling reschedules and running the streets, whilst your staff are sitting around or moving at snail's pace every time I visit. But then you claim you are the ones that are stressed. What about me? You stress me out.
Please tell your staff to never twist what their patients have said and then accuse them aggressively to their face.
